newsitem.title: IRAN: OPEC compliance committee meeting underway in Iran.
newsitem.headline: OPEC compliance committee meeting underway in Iran.

text.p: OPEC's ministerial quota monitoring committee, charged with examining the oil group's output, began work on Wednesday.

The committee is chaired by Iranian oil minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh and includes Nigerian Oil Minister Dan Etete, the current OPEC president, Libya's Abdullah Salem al-Badri and OPEC Secretary-General Rilwanu Lukman.

Ministers declined comment ahead of the meeting, which will examine media estimates showing runaway OPEC production at nearly 27 million barrels per day, or nearly two million barrels per day above the official supply ceiling of 25.033 million bpd.
The two-day meeting replaces one delayed from March.
Indonesia's Ida Bagus Sudjana did not attend the committee meeting on Wednesday.

Venezualan minister Erwin Arrieta was not in Isfahan on Wednesday for the start of the meeting either, but his Energy and Mines Ministry said in a statement Monday that Arrieta was planning to attend the meeting.
He met Aghazadeh in Tehran on Monday.

Analysts estimate that Venezuela is biggest quota buster in the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries. Its March production was estimated at 3.18 million bpd compared with an OPEC quota of 2.359 million bpd.
Total OPEC output in March hit 26.9 million bpd, a Reuters survey of OPEC officials, oil companies and analysts showed.
Higher OPEC production has contributed to the 25-percent downturn in oil prices since the start of the year.
June Brent crude closed in London on Tuesday at $18.07 per barrel.
